Subject: Follow-up: competitive eval & incident response comparison — next tests and SLAs

Hi Chris,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about Acme's latency and high-availability constraints for your inference routes. Per our discussion, I attached a short competitive matrix that highlights where Redwood's Dedicated/Dedicated+Private options differ from hyperscaler managed endpoints (e.g. AWS SageMaker endpoints and other inference APIs) specifically on incident response, RCA cadence, and escalation paths.

Quick summary here:
- Dedicated capacity with SLA-backed latency windows vs best-effort public endpoints.
- Built-in automatic fallback to lower-cost compatible variants to preserve availability during incidents.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours), Premium (24x7 P1 support with 1-hour initial response), and Enterprise (SLA-backed incident response + named engineer).
- RCA expectations: preliminary incident notes within 4 hours for P1, draft RCA within 72 hours, final RCA and timeline for remediation within 7 calendar days (scope-dependent).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-competitive-matrix-20260505.pdf, redwood-support-sla-rubric-20260505.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi and Neha to provide concrete SLA & RCA examples (I'll loop them in).
2) If useful, run a short failover/latency test against a pinned Dedicated pool (10k tokens/day trial) and share telemetry.
3) Align on exactly which incidents you're most concerned about (KV cache invalidation, disk/GPU preemption, networking blips) so we can simulate appropriately.

Would love to schedule a follow-up next week — are you available Thu 5/7 or Fri 5/8 PST for ~30 minutes?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Chris — quick answers and what we can commit to: 

1) Premium P1 behavior: the 1-hour window is the initial response SLA (ack + triage). For remediation sequencing we provide a defined runbook and immediate mitigation options where applicable (we can invoke automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or route to pre-warmed Dedicated pools). In practice, mitigation actions (e.g., failover) are typically executed within the first 1-3 hours depending on root cause. The Enterprise tier includes a contractual remediation SLO for certain incident classes — we can share language in the SOW.

2) RCA examples: attached is a redacted RCA from a P1 caused by a GPU preemption during a large batch job; it includes timeline, root cause, mitigation steps, and post-incident remediation plan. Preliminary notes are issued within 4 hours; draft RCA within 72 hours; final RCA within 7 days (extended in complex cases).

3) Test harness: we recommend running the following against a pinned Dedicated pool:
   - Step A: Warm KV cache with representative prompts (simulate typical session lengths).
   - Step B: Invalidate KV cache programmatically to emulate node restart/GPU warmup.
   - Step C: Send a mixed distribution of small/large prompts (10k tokens total) and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and CPU/GPU metrics.
   - Step D: Trigger a preemption simulation (our tool will artificially throttle GPU on one node) to measure failover time to the fallback pool.

We can provide a small harness repo and telemetry dashboard (Datadog dashboard link included below) so you can reproduce locally. If you'd like, we can run the test jointly and capture logs for the RCA.

Attachments: redwood-p1-gpu-preemption-rca-redacted-20260506.pdf
Related link: https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/r/incident-runs

—Rishi
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Hi Chris — a few operational details from Support Engineering: 

- RCA scope: our RCAs include timeline, root cause analysis (with tracing/heap profiles where available), mitigation steps taken during the incident, and a follow-up remediation plan. If the incident affects customer data or access, we include a data exposure assessment.
- Escalation path: P1 -> On-call engineer (immediate) -> Support lead (30-60 min) -> Engineering SWAT (if not mitigated in 2 hours) -> Exec notification for multi-customer impact.
- Evidence we can provide for your procurement/security review: audit logs, SOC 2 control matrix excerpt, KMS integration notes, and sample RCA (all redacted).
- For the failover/KV test: we'll provide a test runbook and a temporary pinned Dedicated pool for a 48-hour window (subject to approval). We'll collaborate on the exact prompts and telemetry tags so the results are comparable to your production workload.

I'll upload the runbook and a sample redacted RCA to the shared Drive and post the link in the call notes.
